newsitem.title: USA: Stocks tumble under pressure from rising interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Stocks tumble under pressure from rising interest rates.

text.p: Stocks tumbled Friday as investors sold off under the mounting pressure of surging interest rates propelled by fresh inflation worries.
The Dow Jones industrial average slid 156.78 points to 8,031.22. It was the ninth-largest point decline ever for the blue-chip average.
In the broader market, decliners beat advancers 2,456 to 526 on heavy volume of 561 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange. For the week, the Dow fell 162.82 points.
As on Thursday, when the Dow fell 71 points, stocks got hurt Friday by weakness in the bond market, where the yield on the 30-year Treasury jumped to 6.64 percent from 6.53 percent.

"The two props to valuation levels in this market have been interest rates, which have been trending lower, and earnings, which have been surprisingly good," said Charlie Crane, chief market strategist at Key Asset Management.
"This month, at least so far, we have had the bond market reversing course and nothing sufficiently positive to hold the market up," he said.
The rapid turnaround in interest rates has come amid a sudden flurry of signs that economic growth may have started to accelerate after a tame second quarter.
The evidence, found first in manufacturing and employment reports last week, has sent the long-bond yield up from an 18-month low of 6.31 percent a little more than a week ago.
Investors, with profits from a four-month, 29 percent Dow rally, moved to take them Friday and the selloff at one point sent the Dow down 212 points.
"The markets have done so well lately," said Marshall Acuff, portfolio strategist at Smith Barney. "It doesn't take much to trigger profit-taking."

With little in the way of earnings news, analysts said markets in the coming days would resume their obsessive search for any sign of accelerating inflation. Wholesale and consumer price reports are both due next week.
Rising interest rates hit financial shares hard. Among banks, NationsBank Corp. fell 2-5/8 to 66, BankAmerica Corp. slid 2-1/16 to 68-1/4, and Citicorp dropped 2-1/4 to 134.
Among individual issues, Heritage Media Corp. climbed 2-3/16 to 19-1/16 on news that the Justice Department would not oppose the company's acquisition by Australian media conglomerate News Corp. Ltd.
Electronic Data Systems Corp. slid 6-1/16 to 37 after the computer services company posted weaker-than-expected earnings that prompted a wave of rating downgrades by brokerages.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks fell 17.65 points to 933.54, for a loss of 13.6 on the week. The Nasdaq composite index slid 25.66 to 1,598.52, but rose 4.19 from last Friday.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 8.83 to 483.79, for a loss of 7.19 on the week. The average price per share lost 82 cents.

The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues, also known as the Wilshire 5,000 -- ended at 8,881.84, down 155.26, or 1.72 percent. The index was down 95.744 on the week.
